explanation: The ECU compared the upstream and downstream oxygen sensor signals and found the catalytic converter is storing less oxygen than expected. The code reports converter efficiency; it does not prove the converter itself has failed — a lazy downstream sensor or an exhaust leak can look similar.

initial_hypotheses.label: Exhaust leak ahead of the downstream O2 sensor
Engine misfire history damaging the catalyst

repairs.label: Replace catalytic converter (bank 1)
repairs.verification: Rescan after repair; the catalyst monitor needs several drive cycles to run. Confirm P0420 does not return and the monitor shows ready.

repairs.label: Replace downstream O2 sensor (bank 1, sensor 2)
repairs.verification: Rescan; confirm the downstream O2 voltage holds steady at cruise and P0420 stays clear over 2+ drive cycles.

repairs.label: Repair exhaust leak ahead of the downstream O2 sensor
repairs.verification: Rescan; confirm fuel trims and O2 sensor behavior normalize and P0420 stays clear.

safety.stop_message: A flashing check-engine light means catalyst-damaging misfire: stop driving — continuing can destroy the catalytic converter.

tests.question: At a steady cruise, log upstream and downstream O2 sensor voltages for 60 seconds. What is the switching ratio (downstream switches / upstream switches)?
At the same steady cruise, what is the downstream O2 sensor's peak-to-peak voltage swing? A healthy converter holds it nearly flat near 0.6-0.8 V.
Any audible exhaust leak, soot marks, or loose hardware ahead of the downstream O2 sensor?
Has this vehicle had recent misfire codes (P030x) or a flashing check-engine light?

title: Catalyst system efficiency below threshold (bank 1)
